record.original_question: Does every graph G with minimum degree at least 4 admit a 2-good partition (S, T), meaning min{delta(G[S]), delta(G[T])} >= 2, whose two class sizes are nearly balanced in the sense that floor(|V(G)|/2) - 2 <= |S| <= |T| <= ceil(|V(G)|/2) + 2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a simple graph H, let δ(H) denote its minimum degree, and for a subset U ⊆ V(H), let H[U] denote the subgraph of H induced by U. A 2-good partition of a graph G is an ordered partition (S, T) of V(G) into two nonempty parts such that min{δ(G[S]), δ(G[T])} ≥ 2. Determine whether the following statement holds: every (finite, simple) graph G with δ(G) ≥ 4 admits a 2-good partition (S, T) with |S| ≤ |T| satisfying

⌊|V(G)|/2⌋ − 2 ≤ |S| ≤ |T| ≤ ⌈|V(G)|/2⌉ + 2.
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is false as stated: the complete graph K_5 has minimum degree 4, yet in any partition (S, T) of its vertex set into two nonempty parts at least one part has size ≤ 2, forcing min{δ(G[S]), δ(G[T])} ≤ 1. Hence no 2-good partition of K_5 exists, contradicting the claimed near-balanced existence.
